questions.q: A Walksnail Avatar air unit is connected to a UART of a flight controller with INAV 9.1. Which port function and `osd_video_system` are needed?
options: Mask 33554432 and AVATAR
Mask 131073 and HD
Mask 2097152 and AVATAR
Mask 33554432 and DJIWTF
questions.explain: MSP DisplayPort in INAV is the bit 1 << 25 = 33554432 (serial.h). AVATAR sets a 53×20 grid. 131073 and HD are Betaflight; 2097152 is the old DJI protocol; DJIWTF is the 60×22 grid for WTFOS.

questions.q: Which `osd_video_system` values in INAV 9.1.0 give the same 53×20 grid?
options: HDZERO, AVATAR and DJIWTF
AVATAR, BFHDCOMPAT and DJI_NATIVE
AVATAR, BF43COMPAT and DJI_NATIVE
DJIWTF, BFHDCOMPAT and DJI_NATIVE
questions.explain: In displayport_msp_osd.c the HD_5320 branch is shared by VIDEO_SYSTEM_DJICOMPAT_HD (BFHDCOMPAT), AVATAR and DJI_NATIVE. HDZERO is 50×18, DJIWTF is 60×22, BF43COMPAT is 30×16.

questions.q: A DJI O3 and goggles whose menu has no OSD type “INAV”. What do you choose in `osd_video_system`, and what do you expect?
options: DJI_NATIVE: the full INAV font
DJIWTF: a 60×22 grid without losses
BFHDCOMPAT: some icons are replaced with “?”
AVATAR: the INAV font is loaded from the flight controller
questions.explain: Without the INAV font in the goggles the compatibility mode is what works: INAV characters are remapped to the DJI font, and those without a match are output as “?” (osd_highlight_djis_missing_font_symbols = ON). A font is not transferred from the flight controller to the goggles.

questions.q: The line `osd_layout 0 12 44 18 V`. What happens to the element on HDZero (`osd_video_system = HDZERO`)?
options: The firmware clamps it to row 17
It is not visible: the grid rows are 0…17
It is visible in column 44, row 18
The CLI rejects the line as an error
questions.explain: The HDZERO grid is 50×18, rows 0–17. The CLI accepts a column and a row of 0–63 and checks nothing; osd.c takes the coordinates as they are and does not move the element.

questions.q: The word 0x2118 came over MSP2_INAV_OSD_LAYOUTS. What position is it?
options: Column 24, row 8, visible
Column 4, row 24, visible
Column 24, row 4, hidden
Column 24, row 4, visible
questions.explain: x = 0x2118 & 63 = 24; y = (0x2118 >> 6) & 63 = 4; the 0x2000 bit is set — the element is visible. (24, 8) comes from the five-bit formula, which in INAV applies only to the old DJI protocol.

questions.q: The OSD ALT 2 mode (from a switch) and a logic condition with operation 32 “Set OSD Layout”, operand 3, are both active. There is no failsafe. Which layout is on the screen?
options: Layout 3
Layout 2
Layout 0
Layouts 2 and 3 alternate
questions.explain: In osdRefresh() the OSD ALT modes are checked before the programming framework flag: ALT 3, then ALT 2, then ALT 1, and only then operation 32.

questions.q: The screen shows feet (`osd_units = IMPERIAL`), and the altitude alarm is needed at 400 feet. What do you write in `osd_alt_alarm`?
questions.explain: The threshold is stored in meters with any osd_units: 400 × 0.3048 = 121.92 m. An upper threshold is rounded down — 121; 122 m is already 400.3 feet. 400 would give the alarm at 1312 feet.

questions.q: A fragment of the configuration of an analog aircraft: there is video in the goggles but no OSD. What is the cause?
options: The value PAL instead of AUTO disables the chip
MSP DisplayPort is assigned to port 5 — the MAX7456 is not used
The receiver on port 0 interferes with the OSD
The MSP bit is missing on port 5
questions.explain: fc_init.c tries MSP DisplayPort first and takes the MAX7456 only if there is no port with FUNCTION_MSP_OSD. Remove function 33554432 from port 5.

questions.q: The line `osd_custom_elements 0 1 0 6 2 0 0 2 5 "bat low"`. When is the element visible, and what does it show?
options: Always; the text and logic condition 6
While GVAR 5 ≠ 0; the text and an icon with code 6
While condition 2 is true; the text and GVAR 5
While condition 5 is true; BAT LOW and GVAR 2 with two digits
questions.explain: The parts: type 1 — text (output in upper case), type 6 value 2 — GVAR 2 with two digits, the third part is empty. Visibility: type 2 — a logic condition, number 5.

questions.q: An HD air unit is connected with one wire: flight controller TX → unit RX. The port and `osd_video_system` are set correctly. What happens to the INAV OSD?
options: The OSD does not appear: the flight controller waits for an MSP request from the unit
There is an OSD, but without VTX power control
The OSD appears 1 s after power-up
The OSD is updated once a second
questions.explain: In displayport_msp_osd.c transmission is enabled by the vtxActive flag, which is set only when an MSP command is received from the unit and is cleared after 1 s of silence. Without the flight controller's RX line it is never set.
